expo.name: NovaFit
expo.//splash: The lavender the logo sits on, so the native launch frame does not flash white before the app can draw its own entrance (see SplashOverlay).

ios.//supportsTablet: iPhone only, for now. An app released with iPad support can never drop it, and Apple reviews it on an iPad; one released without it can add it later. It still runs on an iPad, as a phone app.
ios.//infoPlist: ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption: the app uses only the HTTPS the system provides, and saying so here stops App Store Connect asking about export compliance on every upload. CFBundleLocalizations: tells iOS the app speaks Hebrew - without it a Hebrew phone treats the app as English-only, so the system dialogs it shows come up in English and the layout does not start right-to-left.

infoPlist.NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription: Connect to a smart scale to record your weight automatically.
infoPlist.NSBluetoothPeripheralUsageDescription: Connect to a smart scale to record your weight automatically.

android.//blockedPermissions: expo-audio's library manifest declares the microphone permission for recording, which this app never does. Blocked so a beep does not add a microphone entry to the app's permissions. The camera likewise: expo-image-picker declares it for taking photos, and the profile picture only ever comes from the gallery, through Android's photo picker, which needs no permission.
android.//blockedPermissions2: And three more, for Google Play, which reads a manifest literally. FOREGROUND_SERVICE and FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK come from expo-audio, which can run lock-screen controls as a foreground service; this app plays a beep and never starts one, and Play wants every declared foreground-service type justified with a video of the feature. The services themselves are removed by plugins/withStoreManifest. SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW is in Expo's template manifest for the developer menu's overlay; a release build has no developer menu, and 'display over other apps' is not something to ask a stranger's phone for.
android.//versionCode: Google Play accepts each number once: every bundle uploaded has to carry one higher than any before it, whether or not that upload was ever released. Raise it for each upload. It is invisible to users - what they see is `version`, above.

plugins.//modes: None. This lists what the app may do over Bluetooth on iOS while it is NOT on screen. It only ever talks to a scale while the weigh-in screen is open, and it is the one connecting, never the one advertising - so the "peripheral" that used to be here declared a background mode the app has no use for, which is a standard reason for App Store review to reject a build.
plugins.bluetoothAlwaysPermission: Connect to a smart scale to record your weight automatically.

plugins.//: The sentence iOS shows the first time the entry lock (auth/appLock.ts) asks for Face ID. Without one the system ends the app instead of asking.
plugins.faceIDPermission: Unlock NovaFit with Face ID instead of typing your password.

plugins.//: Playback only: the timed-workout beeps. Nothing in this app records, so it does not ask for the microphone.

Only ever used to choose a profile picture from the gallery. Listed here to say so in the app's own words on iOS, and to switch off the camera and microphone the library would otherwise declare on both platforms - it can take photos and record video, and this app does neither.
plugins.photosPermission: Choose a profile picture from your photos.

extra.//apiBaseUrl: Base URL of the Fastify service that holds the LLM key. Empty until deployed; the coach screen then says it is not configured rather than failing on a bad fetch. For local development use the machine's LAN address, or run 'adb reverse tcp:3000 tcp:3000' and set http://127.0.0.1:3000 — 'localhost' from a phone means the phone.
extra.//supabase: From the Supabase project: Settings -> API. supabaseUrl is the Project URL; supabaseAnonKey is the 'anon public' key (safe to ship — RLS protects data, not key secrecy). Never put the service_role key here; that one bypasses RLS and belongs only in the API service's .env.
extra.//blePermissions: neverForLocation is set on BLUETOOTH_SCAN so Android 12+ does not require the user to grant location just to find a scale. ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION remains declared because Android 11 and below have no BLUETOOTH_SCAN and genuinely gate BLE discovery behind location.
extra.//blePermissionsLegacy: BLUETOOTH and BLUETOOTH_ADMIN were added by the react-native-ble-plx config plugin, not by hand. They are the pre-Android-12 equivalents of BLUETOOTH_CONNECT and BLUETOOTH_SCAN, scoped by the manifest merger to older API levels — inert on Android 12+, required below it.
extra.//healthPermissions: Health Connect permissions are android.permission.health.* and are granted per data type inside the Health Connect app, not by a standard runtime prompt. Only the WRITE set is declared: it is how a finished workout reaches Samsung Health and anything else that reads the store. The five READ permissions (exercise, heart rate, active and total calories, weight) were declared for importing a watch's workout, a feature whose code exists in src/health/reader.ts and which no screen calls. Google Play requires every health permission to be justified by something the app visibly does, so they are out until that import is wired to a screen - at which point they come back here, and into READ_PERMISSIONS' request, together. Android 14 and up also want an activity-alias for the permissions rationale, which prebuild does not add - see native/health/README.md.
extra.//minSdk: Raised from Expo SDK 54's default of 24 to 26 because androidx.health.connect:connect-client declares minSdk 26; below that the manifest merger fails the build outright. 26 is Android 8.0 (2017), and Health Connect is unavailable on anything older anyway, so this drops no device that could have used the watch integration.
